_note: Chapter structure taken from the board's Table of Specifications, not from the 2006 syllabus.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The app's chapter lists were the 2006 nine-unit scheme while the outcomes
are NCP 2022-23, and the two do not line up. Forcing one onto the other left Transfer of Heat
with zero outcomes, Gravitation with two, and all fifteen Electricity and Magnetism outcomes,
16% of the paper, filed under Properties of Matter. The ToS in each Assessment Framework states
how the board actually builds the paper, so that is what a chapter should be.
THE MAPPING IS NOW DETERMINISTIC. A chapter is a domain, or a stated range within one, so every
outcome lands in exactly one chapter by its own code. No model call, no guesswork, and the same
answer every run. `slos` is a list of domain letters or CODE-RANGE strings like 'B:1-15'.
`marks` and `share` are the board's own weightings from the ToS. They are worth surfacing to a
student: knowing Dynamics is 22% of the paper and Modern Physics is 3% is exam strategy.
MARKS ARE NOT PAPER MARKS. Several ToS tables list both branches of every either/or
question, so their columns foot to well above the paper's real total: Physics 108 against
a 48 mark paper, Urdu 87 against 75, Islamiyat 180 against 100. `share` is the number to
trust and to show a student, because the board states it directly. Treat `marks` as relative
weight within a subject, never as 'this chapter is worth N marks on your paper'.
source: ModelPaper/2025/Assessment Frameworks/SSC-I/*, Table of Specification pages

phy._note: Domain B (Mechanics) carries 86 of the 141 outcomes, far too many for one chapter. The ToS splits it into four named content areas, and those ranges partition B1-B86 exactly.

eng.sourcePage: Table of Specification of the Model Paper English SSC-I, content/fbise/text/framework-eng.txt lines 1622-1639 (PDF page 43 of framework-eng.pdf). Domain A (Oral Communication Skills, Details of Content Areas/SLOs table, lines 222-253, PDF page 1) is explicitly marked 'part of regular teaching and learning... isl.sourcePage: Table of Specification (ToS) Islamiat-IX, Model Paper Islamiyat (Compulsory) Grade IX (SSC-I), PDF page 24 of 25 of content/fbise/pdf/framework-isl.pdf (rendered to PNG and read by hand). totalMarks (100) is the paper's own scored total, Section A 20 marks (MCQ) plus Sections B-D 80 marks, matching data/fbise/isl.json paper.totalMarks and the model paper's own cover pages ('کل نمبر 20' then 'کل نمبر 80'). The ToS table's own totals foot to 180, not 100: same reason as the Urdu ToS, its key lists both branches of every OR-choice SRQ/ERQ ('Q2(i/f) 3' and 'Q2(i/s) 3'), double-counting alternative questions by design even though a student answers only one branch. marks on each chapter below are the ToS table's own per-strand figures (columns دائرہ کار اول through دائرہ کار ہفتم, row کل نمبر) and intentionally do not sum to totalMarks. share is null throughout: the ToS gives a فی صد (percent) column only for its three cognitive-level rows (جاننا/سمجھنا/اطلاق, knowledge/understanding/application), not per strand, so no board-stated percentage exists per strand to record. Strand order and titles match data/fbise/isl.json's examUnits/domains (دائرہ کار اول = Strand 1 = domain A, and so on); all seven strands are examinable, Islamiyat has no formative-only strand the way Urdu's سننا/بولنا are.

math._note: The board's Table of Specification for Class 9 Mathematics gives marks per DOMAIN (Numbers and Algebra 41, Geometry 71, Information Handling 23), not per chapter. Those three rows used to sit here with number 1, 2 and 3, and the ingest matches on number, so they landed on Matrices, Sets and Logarithms and told students those chapters were 30%, 53% and 17% of the paper. Matrices is not even examined. Until the board publishes a per-chapter split, Maths carries no weight and the app shows none.

urd.sourcePage: Table of Specification, Model Paper Urdu (Compulsory) Grade IX (SSC-I), PDF page 26 of 27 of content/fbise/pdf/framework-urd.pdf (rendered to PNG and read by hand; the PDF's text layer reports the wrong code points for Urdu script, so pdftotext/the .txt extract cannot be used). totalMarks (75) is the paper's own scored total, read off the part headers on PDF pages 18, 21 and 24 (حصہ اول 15 + حصہ دوم 34 + حصہ سوم 26 = 75; the Part 1 cover states 'کل نمبر 15', the Parts 2-3 cover states 'کل نمبر 60'). The ToS table's own row and column totals foot to 87, not 75: its own key explains why, it lists both branches of every OR-choice question ('Q2(i/f) 2' and 'Q2(i/s) 2'), so alternative questions are double-counted by design, to show the full range of content the paper draws from, even though a student answers only one branch and is scored out of 75. marks/share on each chapter below are the ToS table's own per-domain figures (columns قواعد/زبان شناسی, لکھنا, پڑھنا) and intentionally do not sum to totalMarks. Chapters 4 and 5 (سننا, بولنا) are appended for parity with English's eng-1 (Oral Communication Skills): domains A and B in data/fbise/urd.json, marked wholly formative there, so they carry no marks or share here either.
